facts: Sedona is famous for its striking red sandstone formations that glow brilliantly during sunrise and sunset.
Devil's Bridge is the largest natural sandstone arch in the Coconino National Forest.
The famous red rocks get their vibrant color from a thick layer of iron oxide hematite.
Sedona sits at an elevation of over 4,500 feet, giving runners fresh mountain air and scenic high-desert climate.
Hollywood filmed dozens of classic Western movies here during the mid-twentieth century due to its dramatic landscape.
Local lore holds that Sedona contains powerful energy vortexes believed to promote healing and spiritual meditation.
The area features over 200 miles of scenic trails suitable for hiking, mountain biking, and trail running.
Native American tribes, including the Yavapai and Apache, have deep ancestral connections to this sacred desert region.
Cathedral Rock is one of the most photographed natural landmarks in all of Arizona.
Oak Creek Canyon offers lush green scenery, cool swimming holes, and refreshing shade just north of town.
Sedona is a designated Dark Sky Community, making it an extraordinary place for stargazing after nightfall.
Prickly pear cactus grows abundantly here, inspiring local culinary treats like prickly pear margaritas and candy.
Surrealist painter Max Ernst lived in Sedona, drawing creative inspiration from the surrounding alien red rock landscape.
The Bell Rock trail is a popular, accessible loop offering breathtaking panoramic views of the red rock valley.
Temperatures in Sedona remain surprisingly mild compared to the scorching desert heat of southern Arizona cities like Phoenix.
The Chapel of the Holy Cross is a stunning church built directly into the red rock cliffs.
Sedona hosts the annual Sedona Marathon, drawing runners from around the world to its high-altitude courses.
Ponderosa pine forests near Sedona create a fragrant, cool canopy for high-elevation trail excursions.
Ancient Sinagua cliff dwellings, like Palatki Heritage Site, preserve early indigenous architectural masterpieces nearby.
The town named itself after Sedona Arabella Miller Schnebly, the wife of the early postmaster.
